subject: Post-call traffic intake & POC action plan — RPS / tokens / burst profile
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Graves <alex.graves@novarex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call traffic intake & POC action plan — RPS / tokens / burst profile

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we can lock the PoC window. I captured the items we discussed and a short ask list so we can size capacity and define success criteria.

Summary of intake (as discussed)
- Primary integration: API-based queries from Novarex search service to Redwood hosted endpoints.
- Visible workload types: 1) Live search queries (short prompts, user-facing) 2) Enrichment calls for suggestions (longer prompts) 3) Background batch reranks (scheduled).

What we need from you (please reply inline or attach export)
1) Baseline steady-state RPS and typical concurrency (examples below).
2) Average and P95 prompt/response token lengths for each workload type.
3) Burst windows: frequency, typical peak RPS, expected duration (e.g., 3–5 min).
4) Any SLA targets (p50/p95 latency goals) and hard throughput floors for the PoC.

I attached a tiny sample CSV as a template — traffic_profile_sample.csv — please populate with 2 weeks of representative slices if possible. If you can’t produce historical logs, fill in best-estimate numbers.

Proposed next steps and owners
- Novarex: provide completed traffic_profile_sample.csv and call out the most critical endpoint(s) for the PoC (due by Fri 18 Jun).
- Redwood (Aditya) — baseline perf probe and model recommendation based on the profile (deliverable: perf probe plan, by Tue 22 Jun).
- Redwood (Jordan) — PoC success criteria doc and cost estimate for the reserved window (deliverable: draft by Wed 23 Jun).

Proposed PoC timeline (high level)
- Week 0: Traffic intake + model selection + perf probe design
- Week 1: Baseline probes and tuning (latency targets, batching profile)
- Week 2: Simulated bursts and stability run (24–48h)
- Week 3: Acceptance and handoff (metrics review / billing check)

Success criteria suggestions (we can refine):
- Functional: correctness of outputs for 90% of prompt set (Novarex will provide small eval set)
- Latency: p95 under 500ms for user-facing queries during baseline; p95 under 800ms during defined burst windows (configurable)
- Cost: token-unit cost < agreed threshold (we’ll share a per-token projection)

Attachment: traffic_profile_sample.csv (CSV template, 4 KB)

If that looks right I’ll schedule the intake sync for Thursday morning to walk through the CSV with your infra lead.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
From: Alex Graves <alex.graves@novarex.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@novarex.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call traffic intake & POC action plan — RPS / tokens / burst profile

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming Novarex will fill out the CSV and we can supply a small eval prompt set. Initial numbers below (high level estimates, happy to refine):

Workload A — Search (user-facing)
- Baseline steady RPS: 20–30
- Typical concurrency: 25
- Avg tokens (prompt+response): 220
- P95 tokens: 620
- Burst profile: weekly marketing spikes — peak RPS ~300 for 3–6 min, ~2x concurrency

Workload B — Enrichment (session-based suggestions)
- Baseline steady RPS: 8–12
- Typical concurrency: 10
- Avg tokens: 420
- P95 tokens: 1,200
- Burst profile: unpredictable, occasional campaign-driven bursts to ~200 RPS for 30–90s

Workload C — Batch rerank (non-latency sensitive)
- Scheduled windows only, low concurrency; will be isolated to off-peak where possible.

SLA: For the PoC we’d like to aim for p95 < 600ms for user-facing Search during baseline and p95 < 1.2s during burst windows. If those look feasible we’ll proceed.

I attached a small export slice from last week (sample_traffic_export_20270614.csv) — it’s coarse but should be enough to start. We’ll try to return the full CSV by Fri 18 Jun.

Questions for Redwood before we populate the full export:
- What sample size do you need for the probe to be meaningful? (seconds/minutes of steady RPS vs longer runs)
- Do you have a recommended p95 latency we should aim for in the PoC with the models you anticipate recommending?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Graves
Director, Platform Engineering | Novarex
alex.graves@novarex.com | +1 (650) 555-4412

Attachment: sample_traffic_export_20270614.csv (CSV, 28 KB)

---
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Graves <alex.graves@novarex.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@novarex.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call traffic intake & POC action plan — RPS / tokens / burst profile (owners + next steps)

Aditya / Jordan — forwarding Alex’s initial numbers. Novarex will send the completed CSV by Fri 18 Jun. Please see quick owner assignments and asks below so we can be ready when the file lands.

Aditya (owner: perf probe + model selection)
- Draft a perf probe plan: recommended probe duration, concurrency mix, and token-length sampling strategy. Aim for a minimal meaningful probe that gives stable p95 estimates — suggestion: 10 minutes steady-state run at baseline RPS per workload, plus 3 simulated bursts of the stated peak durations.
- Provide recommended batch size and KV-cache settings for the likely model family.
- Deliverable: perf_probe_plan.md and an initial model recommendation (small matrix with expected p50/p95 ranges) by Tue 22 Jun.

Jordan (owner: success criteria + PoC orchestration)
- Draft acceptance criteria doc with pass/fail thresholds and a short cost estimate for a 3-week reserved window. Include rollback/fallback policy if p95 exceeds target by >2x.
- Coordinate access / API keys and confirm any IP allowlist entries Novarex needs to add.
- Deliverable: poc_success_criteria_v1.docx by Wed 23 Jun.

Cross-team tasks
- I’ll schedule a 30-min intake sync Thu 17 Jun at 10:00 PT to walk Novarex through the CSV and confirm endpoints.
- Link HubSpot record: HS-54217 (I’ll update with attachments).

Temporary notes / answers to Alex’s Qs
- Sample size recommendation: for our probes we typically do a 10–15 minute steady run at baseline to stabilize kernel selection and batching behavior, then 3–5 burst simulations matched to your durations. That usually gives representative p95 numbers.
- Recommended p95 target: we can aim for 400–550ms p95 in baseline for the model families likely to be used; p95 during bursts will depend on how aggressive you want batching vs latency. We’ll give a range in the probe plan.

Attachments for internal work: poa_poc_timeline.xlsx (timeline + milestones) and traffic_profile_sample.csv (template) — I’ll drop both to the HubSpot record after this thread.

Let me know if either of you need additional context before Thu.

—
Irene
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
